newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index surges at noon, eyes H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index surges at noon, eyes H1 results.

text.p: Shenzhen B shares extended their recent rally on Friday morning as investors picked up under-valued issues expected to post strong interim results, analysts said.
The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index jumped 4.15 points or 3.31 percent to 129.75 on turnover of HK$32 million.
The index began its rebound on Thursday after finishing Wednesday at its lowest point so far in 1997 at 120.44 points.
The A share index moved up 5.16 points or 1.36 percent to 385.49 on turnover of 2.2 billion yuan.
"Many B stocks, especially solid-performing companies, are oversold after recent plunges," an analyst said.
"Buying in companies aided by talk of strong interim earnings are lifting the market," he said.
Shenzhen-listed firms must publish their 1997 first-half results by August 30.
Analysts said they expected the B index to sustain the gains in the afternoon as the high-flyers were running strong.
"Sentiment has improved after recent gains, with little selling pressure," a China Guotai Securities trader said.
The A index rose on Friday on the absence of news about a major clampdown, which had been rumoured on Thursday, analysts said.
"All that came out was Foshan's suspension, which wasn't as bad as expected," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
China's Foshan Lighting and Electrical Co Ltd was fined and suspended from trading on Friday for making illegal loans to a bank and a brokerage, the company said in a statement.
"Foshan is no big deal in the markets," the Guotai trader said.
In the B share market, China Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd 2024.SZ was the best performer, soaring HK$0.35 or 9.92 percent to HK$3.88.
In the A share market, Chongqing Yu-Gang Tioxide Co Ltd was the star and rose to its 10 percent limit-up level of 5.72 yuan.
